text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Czech government blocks deal between Dutch natural gas distribution Gasunie and Czech gas company Transgas. (p1)
- Amsterdam Stock Exchange closes lower on third consecutive day. (p1)
- Parliament's standing committee on finance wants to question president of Amsterdam Exchanges and head of bourse watchdog STE. (p1)
- Critics of Amsterdam's plans for building housing estate on six islands in nearby IJmeer lose referendum (p1)
- Number of unemployed in Netherlands fell to 429,000 in January. (p1)
- Publisher Wegener Arcade expects profits growth. (p3)
- Paper and packaging group KNP BT forecasts lower Q1 results. (p3)
- Window coverings maker Hunter Douglas to cut 120 jobs.
VOLKSKRANT
- Ajax Amsterdam wins 3-2 against Atletico Madrid in quarter finals of the Champions League. (p1)
- Newspaper publisher De Telegraaf seeks to take over financial daily Het Financieele Dagblad. (p2)
- Cabinet did not provide enough information on technolease construction between Philips Electronics and Rabobank in 1993. (p3)
- Software firm Polydoc will be first business next week with a listing on the New Market Exchange of the Amsterdam bourse NMAX. (p33)
DE TELEGRAAF
- New TV sets to be 50 guilders more expensive due to new environmental regulations. (p3)
- National police seeks to set up rapid reaction force this year to fight corruption. (p7)
- Cable maker Draka reports 23 pct higher 1996 net at Dfl 80.7 million; company seeks takoever candidates. (p41)
- Wegener Arcade to split its shares 1-5. (p41)
TROUW
- Province of South Holland says expansion of Port of Rotterdam on the second Maasvlakte should be realized. (p3)
- Internet providers criticise Dutch PTT Telecom for misusing monopoly position. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- A quarter of the people on social benefits cheats, according to inspection. (p1)
